# PLAINTIFF'S RESPONSES TO DEFENDANT'S REQUESTS FOR ADMISSION, SET ONE

## 1. Preliminary statement

Propounding Party: Defendant Example Fictitious Property Management Services. Responding Party: Plaintiff
{{person__client}}. Set number: One. Every name, date, and document in this paper is synthetic.

## 2. Responses

RESPONSE TO REQUEST FOR ADMISSION NO. 1:

Admitted.

<!-- /keep -->

RESPONSE TO REQUEST FOR ADMISSION NO. 2:

Responding Party admits that Exhibit A is a true copy of the synthetic lease, except that page 3 omits the handwritten
initials that appear on the original.

REQUEST FOR ADMISSION NO. 4:

Admit that rent was paid on 1 April 2026.

RESPONSE TO REQUEST FOR ADMISSION NO. 4:

Responding Party lacks information sufficient to admit or deny this request after a reasonable inquiry, because the only
record of payment is a sample ledger Responding Party has not been able to locate. On that basis Responding Party denies
the request.

Admit that the synthetic heater stopped working on 3 January 2026.

RESPONSE TO REQUEST FOR ADMISSION NO. 5:

REQUEST FOR ADMISSION NO. 6:

Admit that you did not request repairs in writing.

RESPONSE TO REQUEST FOR ADMISSION NO. 6:

Objection. The request is vague as to the phrase "in writing" and assumes that a written request was required. Subject
to and without waiving that objection, Responding Party responds as follows: Denied. Responding Party sent a synthetic
message on 4 January 2026 and again on 11 January 2026, each of which described the condition and asked for a repair.

RESPONSE TO REQUEST FOR ADMISSION NO. 9:

Denied. The parties agreed by a synthetic exchange of messages on 22 January 2026 that rent for February would be
reduced by one-half while the heater remained unrepaired. Responding Party will produce those messages under a separate
synthetic request for production.
